The reaction is most likely **Boc protection (N-carbamylation) of the secondary amine**.

### Reactant identification
- First component: **di-tert-butyl dicarbonate (Boc₂O)**
- Second component: a chiral **N-methyl secondary amine** containing a tertiary cyclic amine
- Third component: **triethylamine**
- Fourth component: **dichloromethane**, solvent

### Reaction class
**Nucleophilic acyl substitution / amine Boc protection**

Triethylamine serves as an acid scavenger, while dichloromethane is the solvent.

### Reaction center
The Boc group is transferred from Boc₂O to the exocyclic secondary amine:

\[
\mathrm{R{-}NHCH_3 \rightarrow R{-}N(CH_3)C(O)OC(CH_3)_3}
\]

The ring nitrogen is tertiary and has no N–H bond, so it is not the principal site of protection.

### Likely product
**N-Boc-protected amine**

Proposed product SMILES:

```text
CN(C(=O)OC(C)(C)C)[C@@H]1CN(CC2=CC=CC=C2)C[C@H]1C3=CC=C(Cl)C=C3
```

This corresponds to replacement of the substrate’s N–H proton by a tert-butoxycarbonyl group. No exact empirical ORD record was found for this specific reaction, so the product assignment is mechanistic and highly likely rather than database-confirmed.

## Likely transformation

The reaction is **Boc protection of the secondary N-methyl amine**.

- **Boc₂O**: di-tert-butyl dicarbonate, the Boc-group donor  
- **Triethylamine**: base and acid scavenger  
- **Dichloromethane**: solvent  
- The tertiary ring nitrogen has no N–H bond and is not the primary site of protection.

The exocyclic secondary amine,

\[
\mathrm{R{-}NHCH_3}
\]

is converted to the corresponding carbamate,

\[
\mathrm{R{-}N(CH_3)C(=O)OC(CH_3)_3}.
\]

## Predicted major product

**N-Boc-protected amine**

```text
CN(C(=O)OC(C)(C)C)[C@@H]1CN(CC2=CC=CC=C2)C[C@H]1C3=CC=C(Cl)C=C3
```

This product retains the indicated stereochemistry and incorporates the tert-butoxycarbonyl group onto the exocyclic N-methyl amine.
